blindSummary: A self-governing territory of a distant metropolitan state: same-sex marriage has been legal since 2016; the population is tiny and dispersed; public services are thin; there is no documented hostility.
blindOutOfScope: A territory under the metropolitan state's sovereignty; local deviations noted.
blindSourceSummaries: Independent newsroom report (Sept 2024) on the metropolitan state's decade of self-declaration gender recognition - included here because this territory falls under that state's sovereignty; the territory adopted its own self-declaration-based gender-recognition framework in 2016.

International LGBT-rights organisation overview of the metropolitan state (updated March 2026), included because this territory falls under that state's sovereignty: robust protections, self-determined gender markers, SOGISC discrimination protections.

LGBT travel-news archive report (May 2015) on gay life here, past and present: gay life is 'almost a non-event' - low-key, integrated, non-violent; a modest Pride march since 2010; the 1996 same-sex partnership law passed with virtually no debate - a picture of quiet tolerance.
Same May 2015 archive report (alternate URL of the same piece): same content - no marriage-equality campaigns, no anti-gay clergy or politicians; same-sex partnership quietly passed in parliament.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (April 2016): the territory's same-sex marriage law came into effect - it adopted the metropolitan state's legislation, passed unanimously twice (the first bill lapsed due to elections in the metropolitan state); it replaces the 1996 metropolitan-derived partnership law; a senior local clergy leader supported it.

The territory's national broadcaster (Aug 2014): a new national association for lesbians, gays, bisexuals and transgender people founded - aims for political, cultural and social equality; open to family, friends and colleagues as supporters.
